Describe the reasons or results of events or actions in spoken or written texts, in work and social contexts.

Reason Clauses: Due to, because of, owing to
Result Clauses: So … that
Remember, when you want to introduce a reason for a particular situation, you can use these prepositions at the beginning of the clause.

• You use because of before a noun or a noun phrase.
  • Due to and owing to also mean because of. They sound a little more formal, and are therefore more common in professional English rather than conversational.
  • When you want to link a cause with a result, you can use so ... that. You normally use an adjective or adverb after so.
  • Remember than in formal English, you can put So ... that at the beginning of the sentence and put the verb before the object.
I'd say that because of some really hard work the launch was a great success!
There were a few snags due to unforeseen events but we pulled together and we pulled it off.
It was discovered at the last minute that owing to illness, the speaker was unable to attend so we had to arrange for someone else.
He is so well-versed on the subject of social media that he was able to come and speak without much advance notice.
The author was very happy and said that because of the way we handled her launch, she hopes to work with us on her next book.
Report Verbs with Impersonal Passive Construction
When you want to report a fact or belief, you can use a variety of ways to construct your ideas. When you do not want to mention the source of the information, you can use a passive structure.

You can use the structure It + passive verb + that + finite clause.
A finite clause contain a verb which shows tense.

For example:
It was mentioned that the accident occurred at night.
It has been demonstrated that the hypothesis is accurate.
It is suggested that costs should decrease next month.

Thomas was available and it was revealed that he is a very knowledgeable and entertaining speaker.

Ask someone to tell you about an event they attended that was successfully organized and run.
Write down what aspects of the event were successful and the reasons why it was successful.
Write down any aspects of the event that were not totally successful.
Use the information you got to make a checklist of things to do, to organize and host a successful event.
I interview someone about a successful event.
I write notes on what was successful and why it was successful.
I write notes on what was not successful.
I use the information I gathered to make a list of things to do to have a successful event.
